weather_hook: Peak July heat on the Wasatch Front — extended high-UV, high-temperature days that accelerate asphalt shingle aging, dry out and curl older roofs, and expose under-ventilated attics. This is the season Holladay homeowners notice a tired roof and start weighing repair vs. full replacement.
facts: Holladay is a premium east-bench city in the Salt Lake Valley, sitting directly below Mount Olympus and the Cottonwood canyons; ZIP codes 84117, 84121, and 84124.
Neighbors Cottonwood Heights to the south and Millcreek to the north; established, leafy, higher-value residential character.
Very mature tree canopy — large old trees mean heavy shade in places, but also constant organic debris (leaves, needles, seed pods) in valleys and gutters that traps moisture and accelerates decay.
Housing stock skews mid-century ranch and custom/luxury homes, many with 30+ year-old roofs now reaching or past the end of an asphalt shingle's service life; also newer custom infill.
South- and west-facing roof planes take the brunt of summer UV and heat; on the same roof they routinely age years faster than north-facing planes.

Under-ventilated attics are common on older Holladay homes; trapped summer heat bakes shingles from below and shortens their life, and is a leading reason a roof fails earlier than its warranty suggests.
Premium material options fit the market: architectural (dimensional) asphalt shingles, designer synthetic shake/slate, and standing-seam metal, with manufacturer warranties typically 30 to 50 years.
Some Holladay neighborhoods have HOA design controls; a like-for-like replacement usually clears administratively while a visible material or color change can trigger design review.
Elevation and canyon proximity add wind and occasional hail exposure on top of heat, but the dominant summer decision driver here is UV/heat-driven aging.
